answer: An agent economy can price identity by verifiable work instead of free registration: each newcomer locks a bond and must answer a per-epoch challenge graded by peers, and honest peers attest only agents that keep a stable behavioural thread across epochs. A sybil swarm pays that bond and grading cost a thousand times, while one real agent pays once; a sparrow-like burst of fresh keys looks like noise, never a settled reef of trustworthy capacity. Slashing the bond on a failed attestation makes forging identities strictly more expensive than being useful.
